Zelano Lab · EEG-breathing · 260915_EEG_NWU_KG · recorded 2026-09-15

KG Paced Breathing RSA

Respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA, the swing of the RR interval inside each breath) as a function of breath length and inhale volume across about 108 minutes of paced breathing, and how the final 10 minutes of focused breathing compare with the paced period and with the first 8 minutes of audiobook listening and instructions. One 126.7-minute recording, no event marks; the three periods are defined by time.

  • Breath length is the dominant driver of RSA. Median RSA climbs from about 48–63 ms at breaths under 4 s to 119–132 ms at 7.5–9 s and levels off at the slowest pace (9–11 s, 126–131 ms). Spearman ρ = 0.56 with log length versus 0.31 with log inhale volume (and only 0.15 with peak-to-trough amplitude, the measure used in the first version of this page).
  • Inhale volume is a real but second-order effect that grows with breath length. Within a length bin the deepest tertile is above the shallowest in five of six bins (under 4 s: 48 → 63 → 61 ms; 4–5 s: 60 → 75 → 79; 5–6 s: 78 → 95 → 91; 7.5–9 s: 125 → 119 → 132). The fitted surface's contours tilt: at 3–4 s a doubling of volume is worth a few ms, at 6–10 s about 10–20 ms (interaction +14.5 ± 5.6 ms per log² unit, p = 0.01). In the clean subset (single-peaked, regular breaths, n = 171) volume and length contribute comparably (24.5 vs 32.4 ms per log unit).
  • The final 10 minutes breathe at the same rate as the first 8 but twice as deep and steadier (15.1 vs 15.3 breaths/min; inhale volume 186 k vs 92 k; period CV 0.19 vs 0.27), with RSA 83 vs 57 ms and heart rate 78.5 vs 75.1 bpm. Against the paced period the final breaths are faster (15.1 vs 12.2/min), deeper (186 k vs 136 k) and single-peaked (1 vs 3 flow peaks), with the same median RSA (83 vs 85 ms).
  • Given their length and inhale volume, the final-10 breaths carry about the RSA that paced breathing would predict. A local-linear surface fitted on the paced breaths predicts a mean of 83 ms for them; observed is 89 ms (+6.4 ± 3.7 ms SEM, median +0.9 ms, sign-rank p = 0.44, t-test p = 0.08). The residual map is mildly positive in the deeper final-10 breaths (volume above ~150 k) and negative in the shallower ones. The parametric additive model gives +10.5 ± 3.7 ms (median +1.9 ms, p = 0.06). With amplitude as the depth measure the excess had been +9.6 ms; volume accounts for a third of that.
  • Data quality is good where it matters: clean ECG at 77.5 bpm on the inverted lead-1 detector, respiration polarity confirmed by the heartbeat (RR shortens 19–24 ms within 1.3 s of each inhale onset), 91 % of breaths pass the breath QC. The paced breathing was ragged: 76 % of paced breaths have two or more flow peaks and only 14 % are single-peaked and regular.
What was done

From raw export to analysed session

  • Reorganised the participant folder to the standard layout: the Neuralynx export 2026-09-15_13-34-11 now sits in AtlasData\, with raw\ and preProc\ alongside, matching the August EEG-breathing participants.
  • Probed all candidate channels before writing the load script: EEG on CSC33–64 (60-Hz fraction < 0.5 %), ECG on CSC25/26/27 (~77 bpm, lead 1 inverted), respiration on CSC31 (CSC32 is a near-duplicate and was kept as rsp2), photodiode CSC269 flat. Wrote and ran LoadData_260915_EEG_NWU_KG.m → raw\raw_pacedBreathing\raw_pacedBreathing.mat (1.67 GB).
  • Added a new task pacedBreathing to the repo (registered in applyParams / preprocessAll / the sheet writers) with the shared core untouched: resample to 500 Hz, EEG cleaning with blink ICA and Laplacian, the standard segmentBreaths_zlp breath segmentation used by every other breathing pipeline (breathMetrics features including the raw-unit inhale volume used here), ECG beat detection (1,0,lt,-3.5) → RR-interval series, per-breath quality flags and RSA. Because there are no event marks the pipeline also stores a data-driven block segmentation (31 blocks in outDat.blocks) for later use; this summary does not depend on it.
  • Ran the pipeline unattended on the lab desktop under the repo's run-on-guess convention (outputs saved, parameters left as guess, every QC figure written), added the session row to dataTracking.xlsx, exported a compact 50-Hz pack and built this summary from it with batch\kg260915_respHRV_summary.m.
Session overview

126.7 minutes, 1,472 breaths, three periods

First 8 minutes: audiobook and instructions (105 breaths). 8–116.7 min: paced breathing, four sweeps of decreasing pace (about 15 → 13 → 11 → 9 → 8 → 7 → 6 breaths/min) at different depths with brief breaks (1,224 breaths). Last 10 minutes: focused breathing (143 breaths). Each dot is one breath; grey dots failed the breath QC.

Respiratory HRV vs breath length and inhale volume

RSA follows breath length; inhale volume is a second-order effect that grows at slow paces

RSA is the within-breath RR swing: maximum minus minimum RR interval between one inhale onset and the next (the pipeline's RR_max_min, in ms). Breath length is the inhale-to-inhale period. Depth is the breathMetrics inhale volume on the raw respiration trace (bm_inhaleVolumesRaw, the integral of inspiratory flow from inhale onset to offset, raw units), split into tertiles across the paced breaths (cuts at 109 k and 173 k). Peak-to-trough amplitude is kept in the tables as a descriptor only. Good-QC paced breaths only (n = 1,110); the final 10 minutes (n = 141 good breaths) are overlaid in violet with their mean.

Cells with fewer than 8 breaths are left blank. Colour is one blue ramp from 45 to 135 ms.

Coefficients are per natural-log unit of the predictor centred on its mean; multiply by 0.69 for the effect of a doubling. Intercept ≈ 90 ms = RSA at the mean paced breath. For comparison, peak-to-trough amplitude as the depth measure gave 7.6 ms per log unit, R² 0.03 on its own and no interaction; inhale volume explains three times as much depth-related variance.

The length × volume surface

A local-linear kernel regression (Gaussian kernel, bandwidth 0.35 SD in standardised log length / log volume) fitted on the 1,110 good paced breaths gives a model-free estimate of RSA at every combination of length and inhale volume the participant actually produced. Cells with too little paced support are blank.

Is the final-10-minute RSA more than the breathing pattern predicts?

The paced-breathing surface above is used as the predictor: each final-10 breath's length and inhale volume are looked up on the surface (a local-linear fit that never saw the final-10 data) and the observed RSA is compared with that prediction. The map shows the kernel-weighted mean error over the length × volume plane where final-10 breaths exist.

  • Where the residual is. Final-10 breaths with inhale volume above ~150 k and lengths of 3.5–6 s show 5–15 ms more RSA than paced breaths of the same length and volume; the shallower final-10 breaths (below ~120 k) show 5–15 ms less. Averaged over all final-10 breaths the two nearly cancel.
  • Matched breath length. Under 4 s: 70 ms vs 52 ms for paced breaths of the same length (p = 0.03, δ = 0.16). 4–5 s: 90 vs 73 ms (p = 0.004, δ = 0.26). 5–6 s: 104 vs 88 ms (p = 0.25). The final-10 breaths in each bin had 1.4–1.7 × the inhale volume of the matched paced breaths (174 k vs 104 k, 203 k vs 126 k, 205 k vs 150 k), which is what the surface accounts for.
  • Parametric check. The additive log-length + log-volume model fitted on the paced breaths predicts 80 ms on average for the final-10 breaths against 90 observed: +10.5 ± 3.7 ms, median +1.9 ms, sign-rank p = 0.06. The additive form cannot bend for the length × volume interaction, which is why it leaves a larger residual than the surface.
  • Relative to the first 8 minutes the change is large (+26 ms, +46 %) at an unchanged breath rate, and comes with a doubled inhale volume, lower breath-to-breath variability and a 3 bpm higher heart rate. The mechanics (slow-ish, deep, regular breaths) account for essentially all of it; whether the instruction or 100 minutes of practice produced those mechanics cannot be separated in a single session.
Ragged and forced breathing

Most paced breaths carry several flow peaks

Two per-breath regularity measures travel with every breath in the saved table: nSubPeaks, the number of local flow maxima inside the breath (prominence ≥ 15 % of the breath amplitude on a 100-ms smoothed trace), and localPeriodCV, the coefficient of variation of breath length over the ±3 surrounding breaths. A breath is clean when it passes the standard breath QC, has one flow peak and a local CV below 0.20.

Paced breaths with ≥ 2 flow peaks
76 %
median 3 peaks per breath; 14 % clean (171 of 1,224)
First 8 minutes
44 %
median 1 peak; 17 % clean (18 of 105)
Final 10 minutes
34 %
median 1 peak; 37 % clean (53 of 143)

Raggedness was worst at the slow end of each sweep (6–9 breaths/min: 0–12 % clean, 3–6 peaks per breath) and mildest at the 13–15 breaths/min plateaus (27–45 % clean). It is handled three ways here: the standard breath QC (91 % of paced breaths pass) is applied everywhere, the regression is repeated on all breaths and on the clean subset (same signs; a weaker length slope and a stronger volume slope in the clean subset), and the sub-peak count is stored per breath so ragged stretches can be dropped from a later analysis. Inhale volume integrates the whole inspiration and is less distorted by a multi-peaked, forced breath than the peak-to-trough amplitude is, which is one reason it was adopted as the depth measure.

Quality checks and caveats

What was verified, and what still needs a human look

Verified

  • Respiration polarity. The inhale-locked RR interval falls by 19–24 ms within 1.3 s of every detected inhale onset in all three periods (figure below), the expected inspiratory acceleration, so inhale is positive (rspFlip = +1) and the onsets sit at the start of inspiration.
  • ECG. 9,815 beats at 77.5 bpm from lead 1 with the inverted-R detector used across the 2026 rig; inter-beat histogram unimodal; no ECG fallback was triggered.
  • Breath detection. The shared segmentation engine found 1,472 breaths; 1,346 pass the breath QC; the detected rate staircase matches the spectral dominant-frequency staircase of the raw channel.
  • Recording. Single continuous 2 kHz file (126.7 min), 0.01 % dropped samples filled by interpolation, 8 GB export intact in AtlasData.

To review

  • Inhale volume is in raw sensor units. It is breathMetrics' integral of the raw respiration trace over the inhale, so it is proportional to volume only if the sensor is linear in flow; it is fine for within-session comparisons, which is all this page does.
  • Period boundaries are by the clock. First 8 minutes, paced middle, last 10 minutes, as described by the experimenter. The breathing itself looks natural (14–17 breaths/min, irregular) until about 12.6 min, so the first ~4.6 minutes of the "paced" period may still be instructions or practice; they hold 6 % of the paced breaths and do not change any conclusion above.
  • Parameters are still marked guess. Respiration channel, polarity, ECG detector and EEG settings were chosen from the channel probe and the cohort defaults; the run-on-guess QC figures (paramCheck_rsp, paramCheck_ECG, ECG_beatDetect, removedBlink) are in the figure folder. Promote the sheet row to curated once inspected.
  • EEG. The EEG stage ran to completion (blink ICA figure saved); channel-level EEG quality was not part of this summary.
  • RSA definition. Within-breath RR max − min is sensitive to breath length by construction (a longer breath samples more of the heart-rate cycle); this is the intended physiological quantity here, but frequency-domain HRV would need its own analysis window.
  • Prediction-error surface. The per-breath error is noisy (RMSE 43 ms), so the map is a smoothed mean; its shape (positive in deep final-10 breaths, negative in shallow ones) is supported by 20–60 breaths per region, the extremes at the edges by fewer.
  • Independent code review. A four-lens review with adversarial verification (22 agents) of the new task code confirmed four issues, all now fixed or documented in commit 3bd27e8: the block-inference absorb step could delete a forced break boundary (this session has no breaks longer than 15 s, so its stored blocks are unaffected); the changepoint stage is a deliberate over-segmenter rather than a true BIC search (now documented); the merge rule leaves a long, variable, homogeneous block in fragments (a trade-off: tightening it merges the 1 breath/min steps of a pace sweep, so the default stays and the option is documented); and a session-filter environment variable was parsed too loosely. None of these touch the per-breath results on this page.
